repairs.before: Yao Hong, courtesy Yuanzi, was Yao Xing's firstborn.
repairs.after: Yao Hong, whose courtesy name was Yuanzi, was Yao Xing’s eldest son.

repairs.before: He was dutiful, gentle, and kind, but had no talent for governing a realm, and he was often ill—so Yao Xing long hesitated before naming him heir.
repairs.after: He was dutiful to his parents, affectionate toward his brothers, generous and mild. But he lacked the ability to govern and was often ill, so Yao Xing hesitated over making him heir.

repairs.before: He was filial, friendly, generous, and mild, yet lacked the ability to order the age, and moreover often fell ill; Xing was about to make him heir yet hesitated.
repairs.after: He was filial, affectionate toward his brothers, generous and mild, yet lacked the ability to govern the realm and was often ill. Xing intended to make him heir but hesitated.

repairs.before: Wang Shang, Duan Zhang, and Fu Yunwen tutored him in the classics; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi kept him company over belles-lettres.
repairs.after: Wang Shang, a master of writing, Duan Zhang, a gentleman of the Yellow Gates, and Fu Yunwen, a gentleman of the Department of State Affairs, tutored him in the classics. Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi joined him for literary gatherings.

repairs.before: Director Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and Director Gentleman Fu Yunwen attended lectures with Confucian learning; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi gathered in literary companionship.
repairs.after: Master of Writing Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and gentleman of the Department of State Affairs Fu Yunwen attended him as lecturers on Confucian learning. Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi joined him in literary gatherings.

repairs.before: Director Wang Min and aide Guo Bo thought the laws too soft and pressed for crackdowns. Yao Hong replied: "Humiliate people and you breed defiance.
repairs.after: Wang Min, a master of writing, and Guo Bo, the right assistant director, thought the administration of punishments too lenient and proposed stricter regulations. Yao Hong replied, “Humiliate people and you breed defiance.

repairs.before: You help run the court—widen the path of mercy, not the jailer's whip; harshness is no way to steady ruler and people."
repairs.after: You gentlemen help guide the court and make its principles of government known. If you neglect humanity and clemency and seek only strict laws and cruel punishments, how can you keep the ruler secure and govern his subjects?”

repairs.before: After that, every prince who met a tutor bowed as he had done.
repairs.after: After that, dukes and marquises all bowed when they met their tutors.

repairs.before: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang with palace guards from the heir's residence; Liu Jue was executed and the rest pardoned.
repairs.after: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang, the General Who Guards the Army, to lead the Eastern Palace guards against Liu Jue. Jue was beheaded and the remaining rebels pardoned.

repairs.before: His generals said: "Your victory was swift—publish a victory notice and show the heads to steady the realm."
repairs.after: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness devised your plans with lightning speed and swept away the vile rebels. You should issue an open dispatch reporting the victory and claiming a greater number of enemy heads, to reassure people far and near.”

repairs.before: The generals all urged Hong, saying, "Your Highness's divine calculations strike like lightning; you have swept away the vile rebels—it is fitting to issue a public bulletin reporting it, broadly display their heads, to comfort feeling far and near."
repairs.after: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness’s inspired plans flashed forth like lightning and swept away the vile rebels. You should report the victory in an open dispatch, inflating the tally of severed heads to reassure people far and near.”

repairs.before: I mishandled the pacification and fed rebellion—I should blame myself, not strut and deepen my fault."
repairs.after: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”

repairs.before: I failed in pacification and control, thereby growing traitorous bandits; I ought to take blame on myself and assign guilt among the ranks—how dare I overmuch boast and swagger, thereby adding to the burden of fault!"
repairs.after: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”

repairs.before: Wei Hua told Murong Zhu: "The crown prince's humility is the dynasty's luck."
repairs.after: Hearing of this, Wei Hua, the right vice-director, told Murong Zhu, governor of Henan, “The crown prince truly is respectful and kind. That is a blessing for the state.”

repairs.before: His brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.
repairs.after: His younger brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.

repairs.before: Yao Shao backed Yao Bi, but Yao Hong still trusted him as kin and showed no distrust.
repairs.after: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted Shao wholeheartedly, treated him with the deference due a senior kinsman and bore him no grudge on that account.

repairs.before: Yao Shao often acted as wings for Bi; Hong also gave him whole-hearted clan duty and did not take it as suspicion.
repairs.after: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted Shao wholeheartedly, treated him with the deference due a senior kinsman and bore him no grudge on that account.

repairs.before: Once Yao Hong took the throne he gave Yao Shao real command; Shao repaid him with loyalty unto death.
repairs.after: When Yao Hong claimed the imperial throne, he entrusted Yao Shao with military command. Moved by this, Shao pledged himself to Hong and remained loyal to the end.

repairs.before: Yao Yin, Yin Yuan, and their fellow plotters were put to death.
repairs.after: Yao Yin, Duke of Nanyang, Grand General Yin Yuan and others plotted rebellion. Yao Hong put them all to death.

repairs.before: Yao Hong announced the death, and in the twelfth year of Yixi claimed the throne, declared a general amnesty short of capital crimes, adopted the era Yonghe, and mourned in a hut beside the council hall.
repairs.after: Yao Hong announced the mourning. In the twelfth year of Yixi he claimed the imperial throne, issued a general pardon extending even to those condemned to death, changed the era name to Yonghe and took up quarters in a mourning hut at the council hall.

repairs.before: Hong issued mourning; in the twelfth year of Yixi he presumptuously assumed the imperial seat, greatly pardoned all short of capital crime, changed the era to Yonghe, and lodged in a mourning hut at the consultation hall.
repairs.after: Hong announced the mourning. In the twelfth year of Yixi he presumptuously ascended the imperial throne, proclaimed a general pardon extending to those condemned to death, changed the era name to Yonghe and lodged in a mourning hut at the council hall.

repairs.before: After the funeral he took the reins himself, promoted every official a grade, and invited blunt counsel on what helped or hurt the state.
repairs.after: After the burial Hong took charge of government himself and promoted every official at court and in the provinces by one rank. He ordered civil and military officers alike to speak freely about policies unsuited to the times and measures that would bring honor and benefit to the dynasty, holding nothing back.

repairs.before: Their chief Dang Rong then bolted for home; Yao Hong sent Yao Zan against him.
repairs.after: The Qiang chief Dang Rong then led his followers in revolt and set out for home. Yao Hong sent Pacifying General Yao Zan to attack him.

repairs.before: Dang Rong yielded; Yao Hong moved the head families to Chang'an and let the rest go home to Li-run.
repairs.after: Dang Rong surrendered. Yao Hong moved several hundred of the leading households to Chang’an and sent the rest back to Lirun.

repairs.before: Mao Yong of Beidi seized the Zhao stockade in revolt; Yao Shao captured him.
repairs.after: Mao Yong, governor of Beidi, occupied the Zhao clan’s stockade in revolt against Yao Hong. Yao Shao attacked and captured him.

repairs.before: Adviser Wei Zong, a troublemaker, told Yao Xuan: "The new ruler lacks prestige; Helian Bobo is too strong—the capital's troubles are not over.
repairs.after: After the troops had set out, Yao Xuan’s adviser Wei Zong, a deceitful flatterer who delighted in disorder, urged him, “The ruler has only just taken the throne, and his authority is not yet established. Helian Bobo is powerful, and his incursions are sure to cause great harm. Our court’s troubles cannot yet be put to rest.

repairs.before: You hold the western shield—think hard.
repairs.after: Your Highness has the duty of protecting the ruling house. You should consider this carefully.

repairs.before: Xingwang is a natural fortress commanding three approaches—seize it in earnest and you secure the west and maybe build a power base."
repairs.after: Xingwang is naturally defensible and commands the approaches from three directions. If you occupy it and govern the people there with an open mind, you can secure your position as a bulwark of the dynasty and even lay the foundations of a hegemon’s or a king’s rule.”

repairs.before: Yao Xuan marched thirty-eight thousand households south from Li-run to fortify Xingwang.
repairs.after: Yao Xuan abandoned Lirun and led thirty-eight thousand households south to hold Xingwang.

repairs.before: When Yao Xuan left, the Qiang seized Li-run; Yao Shao smashed them.
repairs.after: Once Yao Xuan had moved south, the Qiang groups occupied Lirun in revolt. Yao Shao advanced against them and defeated them.

repairs.before: Yao Xuan surrendered to Yao Shao, who killed him in fury.
repairs.after: Yao Xuan went to Yao Shao to acknowledge his guilt. Shao killed him in anger.

repairs.before: Earlier Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to recall Yao Xuan; Fosheng instead backed the defection.
repairs.after: Earlier, when Yao Xuan was at Xingwang, Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to reason with him. Fosheng ended up supporting Xuan’s plan.

repairs.before: He decreed pensions and perpetual exemptions for families of soldiers who died in royal service.
repairs.after: Yao Hong decreed that soldiers who died in royal service should receive posthumous titles and their families should enjoy perpetual exemption from levies.

repairs.before: Yao Zan objected to raising sixteen household officers to noble rank: "The heir's staff owes loyalty by duty—they have done nothing spectacular yet."
repairs.after: Hong proposed making sixteen palace officers viscounts or barons under the five-rank system of nobility. Yao Zan objected, “Surely the crown prince’s civil and military officers owe him loyalty as a matter of duty. They have shown no conspicuous merit. Why grant them so many fiefs?”

provenance.reason: 五等 explicitly names the five-grade nobility framework as well as the two ranks 子男; the accepted literal already includes this. This is the only 五等 occurrence in this chapter.

repairs.before: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as fifth-rank barons and viscounts; Yao Zan remonstrated, saying, "Eastern-palace civil and military naturally ought to have the loyalty of guarding unto death—they have not yet had blazing manifest merit; how can they receive so many enfeoffments?"
repairs.after: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as viscounts and barons in the five grades of nobility. Yao Zan remonstrated, “The Eastern Palace’s civil and military officers naturally owe it faithful loyalty. They have yet to show conspicuous merit. Why should they receive so many grants of fiefs?”

repairs.before: Yao Hong replied: "Titles exist to reward future service and mark true virtue.
repairs.after: Yao Hong replied, “The court holds out titles to admonish and encourage those who will render service and to give public recognition to outstanding virtue.

repairs.before: I share every grief with my household staff—how could I hoard favors for myself alone?"
repairs.after: I, Yuanzi, have seen my house struck by misfortune. My palace officers shared all these troubles with me. Could I enjoy the good fortune alone without feeling ashamed?”

repairs.before: Yao Shao urged delay: "Reward them, yes, but wait until spring as the ancients would."
repairs.after: Yao Shao stepped forward. “Your Majesty remembers to reward virtue, and you are right to grant them fiefs. In antiquity people treated such matters with reverence, timing the appointments for the beginning of the year. You could wait until next spring and then deliberate.”

repairs.before: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose against Yao Hong, entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, raised the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
repairs.after: Several tens of thousands of Hu households from Bingzhou, Dingyang and Ercheng rebelled against Hong. They entered Pingyang, attacked General Yao Chengdu, who held the title Liyi, at the Xiongnu fort, and proclaimed Cao Hong of the Xiongnu grand shanyu. Everywhere they went they ravaged and plundered.

repairs.before: Several tens of thousands of settlements of Hu in Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against Hong and entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, pushed the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
repairs.after: Several tens of thousands of Hu households from Bingzhou, Dingyang and Ercheng rebelled against Hong. They entered Pingyang, attacked General Yao Chengdu, who held the title Liyi, at the Xiongnu fort, and proclaimed Cao Hong of the Xiongnu grand shanyu. Everywhere they went they ravaged and plundered.

repairs.before: Yao Yi marched from Puban, shattered them at Pingyang, sent Cao Hong to Chang'an, and resettled fifteen thousand elite households in Yongzhou.
repairs.after: Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East, marched from Puban against Cao Hong, routed him at Pingyang, captured him and sent him to Chang’an. Yi resettled fifteen thousand leading households in Yongzhou.

repairs.before: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi from Puban campaigned against Cao Hong, fought at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized Cao Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand notable settlements to Yongzhou.
repairs.after: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi set out from Puban against Cao Hong. He fought at Pingyang, routed Hong, captured him and sent him to Chang’an. He transferred fifteen thousand of their leading households to Yongzhou.

repairs.before: Yang Sheng of Chouqi seized Qishan, captured Wang Zong, and drove on Qinzhou.
repairs.after: Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, stormed Qishan, captured General Wang Zong, who held the title Jianjie, and pressed on toward Qinzhou.

repairs.before: Duke of Chouqi Yang Sheng attacked and took Qishan, seized Jianjie Wang Zong, then pressed Qinzhou.
repairs.after: Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, stormed Qishan, captured General Wang Zong, who held the title Jianjie, and pressed on toward Qinzhou.

repairs.before: Yao Hong sent Yao Ping; Yang Sheng pulled back.
repairs.after: Yao Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to relieve Qinzhou, and Yang Sheng withdrew.

repairs.before: Yao Song and Yao Ping chased Yang Sheng to Bamboo Ridge while Yao Zan brought Yao Qindu and Wang Huan with palace troops.
repairs.after: Yao Song and Yao Ping pursued Yang Sheng and caught up with him at Bamboo Ridge. Yao Zan hurried to their aid with Yao Qindu, governor of Longxi, Wang Huan, governor of Lüeyang, and the palace guards.

repairs.before: Yao Song with Ping pursued Sheng as far as Bamboo Ridge; Yao Zan led Longxi Grand Administrator Yao Qindu and Lüeyang Grand Administrator Wang Huan with household troops to hurry there.
repairs.after: Yao Song and Yao Ping pursued Yang Sheng and caught up with him at Bamboo Ridge. Yao Zan hurried to their aid with Yao Qindu, governor of Longxi, Wang Huan, governor of Lüeyang, and the palace guards.

repairs.before: At Qingshui, Yao Zan learned Yao Song had been crushed—Song, Qindu, and Wang Huan all lay dead.
repairs.after: When Yao Zan reached Qingshui, Yang Sheng defeated Yao Song. Song, Yao Qindu and Wang Huan all died in battle.

repairs.before: Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, then withdrew to Chouqi.
repairs.after: When Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, Yang Sheng withdrew to Chouchi.

repairs.before: Zan reached Qinzhou and withdrew to Chouqi.
repairs.after: When Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, Yang Sheng withdrew to Chouchi.

repairs.before: Earlier a stone drum in Jixian boomed for hundreds of li and pheasants called without cease.
repairs.after: Earlier a stone drum had sounded in Ji county, Tianshui. It could be heard for several hundred li, and the wild pheasants all crowed.

repairs.before: Qinzhou then suffered dozens of quakes, rockslides, and ruined homes—everyone called it an ill omen.
repairs.after: Qinzhou suffered thirty-two earthquakes, eight accompanied by rumbling. Mountains collapsed and houses fell. Everyone took these as ill omens.

repairs.before: Wise men said Qinzhou was Yao Hong's home ground—its ruin foretold his own.
repairs.after: Those who understood the signs thought that, because Qinzhou was Yao Hong’s native place, they foretold his impending downfall.

repairs.before: Those with insight thought Qinzhou was Hong's old homeland—an omen of its about to perish.
repairs.after: Those who understood the signs thought that, because Qinzhou was Yao Hong’s native place, they foretold his impending downfall.

repairs.before: Helian Bobo stormed Yinmi, captured Yao Jundu, and slaughtered over five thousand troops.
repairs.after: Helian Bobo stormed Yinmi, captured Yao Jundu, inspector of Qinzhou, and buried alive more than five thousand officers and men.

repairs.before: Yao Jundu glared and cursed Bobo's cruelty to his face; Bobo slew him in rage.
repairs.after: Yao Jundu glared at Bobo, loudly denounced his cruelty and refused to submit. Bobo killed him in a rage.

repairs.before: After Yinmi, Bobo struck toward Yong and drove every northern household toward Five-General Mountain.
repairs.after: After taking Yinmi, Bobo advanced on Yong. The mixed households north of the ridge all fled to Five Generals Mountain.

repairs.before: Yao Hui quit Anding with five thousand households for Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao blocked him, and he galloped alone back to Chang'an.
repairs.after: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, abandoned Anding and fled toward Xinping with five thousand households. Hu Yan, Hua Tao and others from Anding led their followers against him, and Hui returned to Chang’an alone on horseback.

repairs.before: Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi died fighting Hu Yan; Yao Chen abandoned his post and ran east.
repairs.after: Hu Yan killed the generals Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi, holders of the titles Lijie and Jianwu respectively. Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West, abandoned his garrison and fled east.

repairs.before: Lijie Mijie Cheng and Jianwu Pei Qi were killed by Yan; General Who Guards the West Yao Chen abandoned the garrison and fled east.
repairs.after: Hu Yan killed the generals Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi, holders of the titles Lijie and Jianwu respectively. Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West, abandoned his garrison and fled east.

repairs.before: Yao Shao, Yin Zhao, and Yao Qia led fifty thousand men against Bobo; Yao Hui followed with ten thousand horse.
repairs.after: Yao Shao, General Who Campaigns against the Enemy Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia and others led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry against Bobo. Yao Hui followed with ten thousand picked cavalry.

repairs.before: At Hengshui Bobo pulled back to Anding; Hu Yan shut the gates, killed thousands of Xianbei, and handed the city over.
repairs.after: Shao’s army halted at Hengshui. Bobo fell back toward Anding, hoping to hold it, but Hu Yan shut the gates against him, killed several thousand Xianbei and surrendered Anding to Qin.

repairs.before: Yao Shao beat Bobo at Ma'an Ridge, chased him toward Zhaona, then broke off the pursuit.
repairs.after: Yao Shao pressed after Bobo, defeated him at Ma’an Slope and pursued him as far as Chaona. Unable to overtake him, Shao returned.

repairs.before: Shao advanced the army to tread on Bobo, fought at Ma'an Slope, defeated him, pursued to Zhaona, did not catch up and returned.
repairs.after: Yao Shao pressed after Bobo, defeated him at Ma’an Slope and pursued him as far as Chaona. Unable to overtake him, Shao returned.

repairs.before: Yang Sheng sent his nephew Yang Juan against Changshe.
repairs.after: Yang Sheng sent Yang Juan, his elder brother’s son, to invade Changshe.

repairs.before: The Di chief Gou Ke seized Wuzhangyuan; Yao Wan and Yao Nan marched against him and lost.
repairs.after: Gou Ke, a Di man of Pingyang, gathered more than a thousand men and occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt. Yao Hong sent Yao Wan, General Who Guards the Distant Lands, and Yao Nan, General Who Restores Might, against him. Gou Ke defeated them.

repairs.before: Yao Hong sent Lian Mankui and Yao Guang'er to Chencang; Yang Juan bolted for Sanguan.
repairs.after: Hong sent Lian Manwei, General Who Supports the State, and Forward General Yao Guang’er to attack Yang Juan at Chencang. Juan fled to San Pass.

repairs.before: Hong sent General Who Supports the State Lian Mankui and Forward General Yao Guang'er to campaign against Yang Juan at Chencang; Juan fled to Sanguan.
repairs.after: Hong sent Lian Manwei, General Who Supports the State, and Forward General Yao Guang’er to attack Yang Juan at Chencang. Juan fled to San Pass.

repairs.before: Bobo's nephew Ti raided Chiyang but Yao Yu, Peng Bailang, and She Xuan threw him back.
repairs.after: Bobo sent Ti, his elder brother’s son, south to invade Chiyang. Yao Yu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Forward General Peng Bailang, and General She Xuan, who held the title Jianyi, met his attack and drove him back.

repairs.before: Bobo sent his elder brother's son Ti south to raid Chiyang; chariots and cavalry Yao Yu, Forward General Peng Bailang, and Jianyi She Xuan blocked him and drove him back.
repairs.after: Bobo sent Ti, his elder brother’s son, south to invade Chiyang. Yao Yu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Forward General Peng Bailang, and General She Xuan, who held the title Jianyi, met his attack and drove him back.

repairs.before: Soon Liu Yu of Jin massed at Pengcheng and sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e through Huai-Fei against Qiqiu and Xiangcheng while Shen Linzi struck Cangyuan from Bian.
repairs.after: Soon afterward Jin’s grand commandant Liu Yu led a great army against Yao Hong and halted at Pengcheng. He sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Dragon-Soaring General Wang Zhen’e in by the Huai and Fei rivers to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng. General Shen Linzi entered the Yellow River from the Bian and attacked Cangyuan.

repairs.before: Wang Gousheng yielded Qiqiu to Wang Zhen'e, Yao Zhang yielded Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji, and the Jin host poured through Yingkou almost unopposed.
repairs.after: Hong’s general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Wang Zhen’e, and Yao Zhang, inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji. The Jin army then entered Yingkou, and many places submitted as it advanced.

repairs.before: Hong's general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Zhen'e; Xuzhou Inspector Yao Zhang surrendered Xiangcheng to Daoji; the royal army then entered Yingkou, and wherever it went there was surrender.
repairs.after: Hong’s general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Wang Zhen’e, and Yao Zhang, inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji. The Jin army then entered Yingkou, and many places submitted as it advanced.

repairs.before: Only Dong Zun of Xin'cai held out until Tan Daoji stormed the city and bound him before the camp.
repairs.after: Only Dong Zun, governor of Xincai, held firm and refused to surrender. Tan Daoji stormed the place, had Zun bound and brought him to the gate of the camp.

repairs.before: Dong Zun snapped: "Ancient kings campaigned with courtesy toward worthy foes.
repairs.after: With a stern expression Dong Zun said, “When kings of old made war on other states, they treated men of worth with courtesy.

repairs.before: Zun in stern color said, "Kings of old in campaigning against states treated knights with ritual.
repairs.after: With a stern expression Dong Zun said, “When kings of old made war on other states, they treated men of worth with courtesy.

repairs.before: How dare you wage an unjust war and dishonor a loyal governor?"
repairs.after: How can you wage war unjustly and treat a man of distinction in another state with such discourtesy?”

repairs.before: How can you, sir, march with unrighteous conduct and treat a state's knights without ritual."
repairs.after: How can you wage war unjustly and treat a man of distinction in another state with such discourtesy?”

repairs.before: Yao Shao raced back to warn Yao Hong: "Jin is past Xuchang—Yuzhou and Anding are too far to save. Move frontier households into the capital for a hundred thousand veterans.
repairs.after: Hearing that the Jin army had arrived, Yao Shao returned to Chang’an and told Hong, “Jin has already passed Xuchang. Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and distant. It would be hard to relieve them at short notice. Move the garrison households inward to strengthen the capital region. We could raise a hundred thousand picked troops, enough to range unchallenged throughout the realm.

repairs.before: Liang Xi argued: "Yao Hui terrifies the north; his garrisons hate Bobo and will die before yielding—Bobo cannot skip Anding to strike the core.
repairs.after: Liang Xi, the left vice-director, said, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, is brave and has a formidable reputation. The people north of the ridge fear him. The garrison’s people already bear Bobo a deep grudge and should hold out to the death without wavering. Bobo cannot bypass Anding and raid the distant capital region.

repairs.before: Personnel clerk Yi Heng whispered: "Yao Hui saved you at Guangping yet has never been richly rewarded.
repairs.after: Yi Heng, a gentleman of the Personnel Department, privately told Hong, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, rendered Your Majesty loyal service in the crisis over the Duke of Guangping. Since you took the throne, he has received no special reward in recognition of his devotion.

repairs.before: Personnel Director Yi Heng secretly said to Hong, "Duke of Qi Hui at the Guangping crisis had loyal merit toward Your Majesty; since Your Majesty's dragon flight and succession, there has been no special reward to answer his intent.
repairs.after: Yi Heng, a gentleman of the Personnel Department, privately told Hong, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, rendered Your Majesty loyal service in the crisis over the Duke of Guangping. Since Your Majesty rose like a dragon and succeeded to the throne, no special reward has acknowledged Hui’s devotion.

repairs.before: When Jin reached Chenggao, Yao Guang in Luoyang begged for reinforcements.
repairs.after: When the Jin army reached Chenggao, Yao Guang, General Who Conquers the South, was garrisoning Luoyang. He sent a rider at speed to request relief.

repairs.before: Yao Hong sent Yan Sheng with three thousand horse, Yao Yinan with ten thousand foot to Luoyang, and Yao Yi to Shan ford as a screen.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yan Sheng, colonel of the Yue Cavalry, with three thousand horsemen to the rescue and the Martial Guard commander Yao Yinan with ten thousand infantry to help defend Luoyang. He also sent Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East and governor of Bingzhou, south to camp at Shan Ford in support.

repairs.before: Zhao Xuan warned Yao Guang: "The enemy is on top of us, the people panic, and we are outnumbered.
repairs.after: Guang’s subordinate commander Zhao Xuan urged him, “The invaders have already penetrated deep into our territory. The people are terrified, and our forces are so outnumbered that it will be hard to meet the enemy.

repairs.before: Hold that fortress and Jin will never dare push west of it.
repairs.after: With Jinyong strongly held and our army intact, the invaders from Wu will never dare pass the fortress and march west.

repairs.before: Starve them under your walls without lifting another spear."
repairs.after: Keep them pinned beneath strong walls, and you can wait and take advantage of their exhaustion.”

repairs.before: Yao Guang listened: he sent Zhao Xuan to Bai Valley and Shi Wuhui to Gong to block Jin.
repairs.after: Guang took their advice and sent Zhao Xuan south with over a thousand picked troops to defend the Baigu stockade, and General Shi Wuhui, holder of the title Guangwu, east to garrison Gongcheng and bar the Jin army.

repairs.before: Guang followed them, then sent Xuan leading more than a thousand picked troops south to guard the Bai Valley stockade, Guangwu Shi Wuhui east to guard Gong city, to block the royal army.
repairs.after: Guang took their advice and sent Zhao Xuan south with over a thousand picked troops to defend the Baigu stockade, and General Shi Wuhui, holder of the title Guangwu, east to garrison Gongcheng and bar the Jin army.

repairs.before: Xuan wept and said to Guang, "Xuan has received triple favor from three emperors—what I hold is only death.
repairs.after: Xuan wept and said to Guang, “Three emperors have shown me great favor. All I can do is die at my post.

repairs.before: Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang, and Wulao fell; Tan Daoji rolled forward unchecked.
repairs.after: Meanwhile Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang and Wulao all surrendered, and Tan Daoji and the others advanced swiftly without a check.

repairs.before: Zhao Xuan fought Mao Dezu at Baigu, was overrun and cut down; Qian Jian tried to drag him clear but Zhao said, "I am finished—save yourself."
repairs.after: At Baigu, Zhao Xuan fought the Jin general Mao Dezu and was defeated by superior numbers. He received more than ten wounds and cried out from the ground. His major, Qian Jian, braved the blades to hold him in his arms and wept. Xuan said, “My wounds are grave. You must leave at once.”

repairs.before: Qian Jian said, "If you fall, I fall with you."
repairs.after: Qian Jian replied, “If you do not survive, General, I will die with you. If I left, where would I go?”

repairs.before: Yan Sheng and Yao Yinan stopped cold when they heard Luoyang was lost.
repairs.after: Yan Sheng had reached Xin’an and Yao Yinan had reached Hucheng. Luoyang had already fallen, so they stayed in camp and advanced no farther.

repairs.before: Prince Yao Yi was vain and credulous; Sun Chang urged him to strike Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, and seize the throne.
repairs.after: Yao Yi was mean and treacherous and easily misled by those he trusted. His major Sun Chang, a cunning flatterer who delighted in turmoil and misfortune, urged him to raid Chang’an, kill Yao Shao, depose Yao Hong and set himself on the throne.

repairs.before: Yao Yi marched to Shan ford and scattered state grain to buy tribal loyalty.
repairs.after: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.

repairs.before: Yi accepted it, then led troops to Shan ford, scattered grain to give to Hebei Yi and Xia of every sort, wishing to hollow out state stores, summon and win the peace-with-barbarians Qiang, and plant private favor.
repairs.after: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.

repairs.before: Zhang Chang and Zuo Ya warned: "You are the emperor's uncle on the western front—your fate is the dynasty's fate.
repairs.after: Yi’s Left Regular Attendant Zhang Chang and Attendant Gentleman Zuo Ya earnestly remonstrated with him: “Your Highness is the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother. You bear the weight of regional command and share the state’s safety and danger, its joys and its sorrows.

repairs.before: Yi's left constant attendant Zhang Chang and attendant Zuo Ya firmly remonstrated Yi, saying, "Your Highness, with the closeness of mother's-brother kin, holds the weight of dividing Shaan; safety and peril, rest and sorrow, you share with the state.
repairs.after: Yi’s Left Regular Attendant Zhang Chang and Attendant Gentleman Zuo Ya earnestly remonstrated with him: “Your Highness is the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother. You bear the weight of regional command and share the state’s safety and danger, its joys and its sorrows.

repairs.before: Grain is the root of power, and you are pouring it away.
repairs.after: Grain is the foundation of the state, yet you are giving it away.

repairs.before: Yao Yi had them beaten to death.
repairs.after: In anger, Yao Yi had the two men flogged and killed.

repairs.before: Yao Hong called Yao Shao into the palace for a secret council.
repairs.after: When Yao Hong heard of this, he summoned Yao Shao and others to deliberate in secret in the court hall.

repairs.before: Yao Shao said: "Yao Yi is weak-minded; Sun Chang made him do this.
repairs.after: Yao Shao said, “Yi is narrow in outlook and easily swayed by others. Sun Chang must be the one behind this affair.

repairs.before: Arrest Sun Chang, put Yao Zan in Shan, and I will take Tong Pass—if they obey, Yao Yi can still march east against Jin.
repairs.after: Just send a swift rider to summon Sun Chang, and send Pacifying General Yao Zan to hold the city of Shan. I will go to Tong Pass to direct the armies. If Chang comes in obedience to the edict, I will have Yi lead the troops now available in Hedong to join us against the invaders from Wu.

repairs.before: Only dispatch riders at speed to summon Chang; send General Who Pacifies Zan to hold Shan city; I will go to Tong Pass to command all armies—if Chang comes bearing the edict, I will order Yi to lead Hedong's available troops together to pacify the Wu bandit.
repairs.after: Just send a swift rider to summon Sun Chang, and send Pacifying General Yao Zan to hold the city of Shan. I will go to Tong Pass to direct the armies. If Chang comes in obedience to the edict, I will have Yi lead the troops now available in Hedong to join us against the invaders from Wu.

repairs.before: If they defy the edict, publish their treason and attack."
repairs.after: If rebellion is already under way and they resist the edict, we should proclaim their crime to the realm and sound the drums to attack them.”

repairs.before: He sent Yao Zan, Simo Guofan, and She Xuan to Shan and Yao Lü to Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.

repairs.before: Thereupon he sent Yao Zan and champion major Simo Guofan, Jianyi She Xuan to camp at Shan ford, Martial Guard Yao Lü to camp at Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.

repairs.before: Yao Yi declared himself ruler and tried to ship grain from Xiongnu Fort to his troops.
repairs.after: Yao Yi raised troops, claimed the sovereign title and circulated proclamations to the provinces and commanderies. He sought to move grain from the Xiongnu fort to provision the garrison.

repairs.before: Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yao Yi tried flattery and sent a pledge knife—Chengdu handed it to Yao Hong.
repairs.after: Yao Chengdu, General Who Pacifies the East, resisted him. Yi tried to win Chengdu over with humble words and bind him closely to himself, sending his belt knife as a pledge. Chengdu sent the knife on to Hong.

repairs.before: Chengdu captured Wang Guo and scolded Yao Yi: "As the emperor's uncle you should steady the throne, not plot treason.
repairs.after: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.

repairs.before: Yi also sent swift cavalry Wang Guo leading several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu; Chengdu seized Guo, imprisoned him, sent reproach to Yi, saying, "The enlightened lord, with mother's-brother closeness, received the charge of the pushing-bar wheel; now the altars' peril hangs like a tassel—he ought reverently to toil in worry and assist the royal house.
repairs.after: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.

repairs.before: The imperial ancestors will not bless a traitor.
repairs.after: Instead you harbor treachery and plot to endanger the dynasty. How could the spirits of our three ancestors rest easy over your conduct?

repairs.before: This grain feeds the frontier—what right have you to give it away?
repairs.after: This garrison’s grain is the support of the whole region. What merit have your garrison men shown that you would give it to them?

repairs.before: Wang Guo was a fool's errand; he waits in chains for the axe.
repairs.after: Wang Guo has made matters worse by his needless intervention, like someone drawing feet on a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.

repairs.before: Wang Guo was a snake painting feet—a criminal of the state; he is already imprisoned awaiting the edict to execute him.
repairs.after: Wang Guo added feet to a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.

repairs.before: I am raising loyal troops to meet you on the Yellow River."
repairs.after: I am now rallying loyal men to punish your crime. When the whole army has assembled, I will meet you on the Yellow River.”

repairs.before: He called the garrisons to arms and gathered supplies.
repairs.after: Chengdu sent proclamations to the cities, exhorting them to loyalty and righteousness. He sharpened weapons, fed the horses and levied contributions for the cause.

repairs.before: Thereupon he proclaimed to the cities, urged them with loyalty and righteousness, sharpened weapons and fed horses, and levied righteous rent.
repairs.after: Chengdu sent proclamations to the cities, exhorting them to loyalty and righteousness. He sharpened weapons, fed the horses and levied contributions for the cause.

repairs.before: Thousands in Linjin rose for him.
repairs.after: Several thousand households in Linjin rose in support of Yao Yi.

repairs.before: Yao Shao crossed at Bo ford, crushed the Linjin rebels, and terrified Yao Yi.
repairs.after: Yao Shao crossed at Bo Ford and routed the rebel households of Linjin. Yao Yi and his followers were shaken with fear.

repairs.before: Guo Chun and Wang Nu besieged Yao Yi.
repairs.after: Guo Chun, Wang Nu and other garrison men from Anding led their followers in surrounding Yao Yi.

repairs.before: Yao Shao took Puban, jailed Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang.
repairs.after: Yao Shao entered Puban, captured and imprisoned Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang and others.

repairs.before: On New Year's Day Yao Hong wept before his court as Jin closed in and kin rebelled.
repairs.after: With defections at home and abroad and the Jin army drawing nearer, Yao Hong received his ministers in the front hall on New Year’s morning. He shed tears of grief, and the ministers all wept.

repairs.before: Yao Hui marched on Chang'an with thirty-eight thousand families in chariot fortresses, claiming he would purge evil counselors.
repairs.after: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, burned the houses and led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households toward Chang’an from North Yongzhou, forming his wagons into a square. He styled himself grand commander-in-chief and Great General Who Establishes Righteousness and sent proclamations to the provinces and commanderies declaring his intent to rid the ruler’s side of evil men.

repairs.before: Jiang Ji rode to his banner.
repairs.after: Jiang Ji, General Who Displays Might, led his men to join Hui.

repairs.before: Peng Wandu, who bore credentials, heard that Hui was about to arrive, abandoned Yinmi, and fled back to Chang'an.
repairs.after: When General Peng Wandu, holder of the title Jianjie, heard that Hui was approaching, he abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang’an.

repairs.before: Jianjie Peng Wandu heard Hui would arrive, abandoned Yinmi, fled back to Chang'an.
repairs.after: When General Peng Wandu, holder of the title Jianjie, heard that Hui was approaching, he abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang’an.

repairs.before: Jiang Ji urged Hui, saying, "The state's weighty generals are in the east; the capital is empty—with light troops you could raid straight in; the affair would surely succeed."
repairs.after: When Hui reached Xinzhi, Jiang Ji urged him, “The state’s leading generals are in the east, leaving the capital undefended. If you strike straight at it with light troops, you are sure to succeed.”

repairs.before: Yao Chen lost to Yao Hui; panic gripped Chang'an.
repairs.after: Yao Hui defeated Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West. Hui’s army gathered still greater strength, and Chang’an was badly shaken.

repairs.before: Yao Hong recalled Yao Shao and sent Yao Yu and Hu Yidu west of the Feng River.
repairs.after: Hong sent a rider at speed to summon Yao Shao and ordered Yao Yu and Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to camp west of the Feng River.

repairs.before: Several frontier generals went over to Yao Hui.
repairs.after: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.

repairs.before: Fufeng Grand Administrator Yao Jun, Protector of the Pacified Yi Yao Moli, Jianwei Yao E'du, General Who Displays Might Peng Hao all feared and surrendered to Hui.
repairs.after: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.

repairs.before: Yao Hong summoned Gou He and asked, "Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay—how can you alone remain at ease?"
repairs.after: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”

repairs.before: Hui's maternal uncle Gou He then served as Jianjie general, kept loyalty without wavering; Hong summoned him and said, "The multitude all harbor leaving or staying—how can you alone be at ease?"
repairs.after: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”

repairs.before: Gou He said: "If treason wins, uncle and nephew share the stain.
repairs.after: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.

repairs.before: He said, "If Heaven lets the demon bandit prevail and he gets to carry out his treason, the principle of uncle and nephew needs no guest-retainer to grow closer.
repairs.after: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.

repairs.before: If Heaven punishes the traitor, a subject stands by his oath.
repairs.after: If instead his crimes reach their limit, his rebellion comes to nothing and Heaven visits its full punishment on him, my duty as a subject is to remain loyal and hold to my resolve.

repairs.before: Betraying sovereign for kin would shame me."
repairs.after: To turn against my kin or betray my ruler would shame me.”

repairs.before: Yao Hong honored him with gold seal and purple ribbon.
repairs.after: Hong commended his loyalty and consideration and awarded him a gold seal with a purple ribbon.

repairs.before: Yao Shao raced ahead while Yao Qia and Guofan brought thirty thousand foot toward the capital.
repairs.after: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.

repairs.before: Yao Shao led light horse first to the crisis, sent Yao Qia and Simo Guofan leading thirty thousand foot to hurry to Chang'an.
repairs.after: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.

repairs.before: Yao Hui camped at Ducheng; Yao Shao met him at Lingtai.
repairs.after: Yao Hui advanced from Qulao and camped at Ducheng. He and Yao Shao faced one another at Lingtai.

repairs.before: Yao Zan rushed back from Tong Pass, leaving Yin Ya to hold the river.
repairs.after: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.

repairs.before: When Zan heard Hui pressed gradually, he left Ningyin Yin Ya as Hongnong grand administrator guarding Tong Pass, led all armies back to Chang'an.
repairs.after: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.

repairs.before: Yao Hong told Yao Zan: "I have failed the ancestors and shamed my uncles with these kin revolts.
repairs.after: Hong acknowledged his fault to Zan: “I, Yuanzi, have failed to uphold and make known the way of virtue and righteousness or to lead my subordinates. I have let disaster arise within my walls and rebellion break out among my own brothers. I have failed my ancestors and am ashamed to face my uncles.

repairs.before: Hong thanked Zan, saying, "Yuanzi cannot brighten virtue and righteousness or lead the host below, causing disaster to rise from the inner wall and change to come from same-blood kin—already above I fail the ancestors, below I have no face to see the uncles.
repairs.after: Hong acknowledged his fault to Zan: “I, Yuanzi, have failed to uphold and make known the way of virtue and righteousness or to lead my subordinates. I have let disaster arise within my walls and rebellion break out among my own brothers. I have failed my ancestors and am ashamed to face my uncles.

repairs.before: Yao Zan said, "The reason Yi and others dared raise arms in inner insult is surely because we ministers seemed weak and had no means to check them."
repairs.after: Yao Zan replied, “Yi and the others dared take up arms and attack us from within surely because we, your ministers, are weak and had no means of forestalling or checking them.”

repairs.before: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject and the grand general will not destroy these bandits—I shall never again show my face before Your Majesty!"
repairs.after: Pushing up his sleeves and weeping aloud, Zan said, “Unless the grand general and I destroy this rebel, I will never again show my face before Your Majesty!”

repairs.before: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject with the grand general will not destroy these bandits—never again shall I hold face to see Your Majesty!"
repairs.after: Pushing up his sleeves and weeping aloud, Zan said, “Unless the grand general and I destroy this rebel, I will never again show my face before Your Majesty!”

repairs.before: Yao Hong paid the troops and sent them out.
repairs.after: Yao Hong distributed gifts to the soldiers and sent them off.

repairs.before: Yao Hui's men wavered; Qi Huang and others defected.
repairs.after: When Hui’s men saw that the armies had all assembled, fear seized them and they began to think of returning to allegiance. His general Qi Huang and others abandoned him and surrendered.

repairs.before: Yao Zan fell on Yao Hui from the rear, killed him and three brothers.
repairs.after: As Hui advanced against Shao, Zan intercepted him from the rear and routed him, killing Hui and his three younger brothers.

repairs.before: Yao Hong buried him with princely honors and mourned bitterly.
repairs.after: Yao Hong wept bitterly for Hui and buried him with the rites of a duke.

repairs.before: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi took Xiangyi; Xue Bo ran to Hedong.
repairs.after: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi stormed Xiangyi stockade. Xue Bo, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Hedong.

repairs.before: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi attacked and took Xiangyi stockade; Jianwei Xue Bo fled to Hedong.
repairs.after: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi stormed Xiangyi stockade. Xue Bo, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Hedong.

repairs.before: Tan Daoji crossed north against Puban; Gou Zhuo lost to Yao Chengdu at Xiongnu Fort.
repairs.after: Tan Daoji crossed north from Shan to attack Puban and sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort. Hong’s General Who Pacifies the East, Yao Chengdu, defeated Gou Zhuo.

repairs.before: Daoji crossed north from Shan, attacked Puban, sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort, and was defeated by Hong's General Who Calms the East Yao Chengdu.
repairs.after: Tan Daoji crossed north from Shan to attack Puban and sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort. Hong’s General Who Pacifies the East, Yao Chengdu, defeated Gou Zhuo.

repairs.before: Yao Hong sent Yao Lü to Puban and Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yao Lü to relieve Puban, while Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.

repairs.before: Yao Hong made Yao Shao supreme commander with the yellow axe and Lu dukedom, leaving all war policy to him.
repairs.after: Hong promoted Shao to grand minister, grand general, grand commander-in-chief and commander of all military affairs at court and in the provinces. He granted him the yellow axe and changed his fief to the dukedom of Lu. Shao retained his offices as palace attendant, metropolitan inspector and director of the imperial clan, his staff of authority and his oversight of the Secretariat. All major matters of court policy went to him for decision.

repairs.before: Hong advanced Shao to grand tutor, grand general, grand commander-in-chief, commander of all military affairs within and without, granted yellow battle-axe, changed enfeoffment to duke of Lu—palace attendant, director of Sizhou, director of clan affairs, holding seal and tallies as before; great court policy all went to decide there.
repairs.after: Hong promoted Shao to grand minister, grand general, grand commander-in-chief and commander of all military affairs at court and in the provinces. He granted him the yellow axe and changed his fief to the dukedom of Lu. Shao retained his offices as palace attendant, metropolitan inspector and director of the imperial clan, his staff of authority and his oversight of the Secretariat. All major matters of court policy went to him for decision.

repairs.before: He sent Yao Shao with fifty thousand men to Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yao Shao, with Martial Guard commander Yao Luan and others, at the head of fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose the Jin army at Tong Pass.

repairs.before: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao hit Tan Daoji from two sides.
repairs.after: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao, inspector of Bingzhou, coordinated their forces inside and outside the defenses and attacked Tan Daoji from both sides.

repairs.before: Shen Linzi urged Tan Daoji, saying, "Puban is walled and moated too strong for a quick assault; attacking bleeds the army, holding it wastes days. Abandon it and strike Tong Pass first.
repairs.after: Tan Daoji stayed behind his fortifications and declined battle. Shen Linzi urged him, “Puban’s walls are strong and its moat is deep. We cannot take it quickly. An assault would cost us men, and waiting here would waste days. Better abandon it and turn first to Tong Pass.

repairs.before: Tan Daoji gave up Puban and marched on Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Tan Daoji followed his advice, abandoned Puban and headed south toward Tong Pass.

repairs.before: Yao Zan took seven thousand palace guards to Pu ford.
repairs.after: Yao Zan led seven thousand palace guards east from north of the Wei River and advanced to occupy Pu Ford.

repairs.before: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo; towns collapsed toward the capital.
repairs.after: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo with more than ten thousand men. In many places people abandoned their cities and garrisons and fled to Chang’an.

repairs.before: Shen Tianzi reached Qingni while Yao Shao advanced to face Tan Daoji.
repairs.after: Shen Tianzi and the others advanced as far as Qingni, while Yao Shao advanced in square formation to bar Tan Daoji’s way.

repairs.before: Daoji led Wang Chong, Shen Linzi and others to charge straight at Shao's army; officers and soldiers startled and scattered, drew back to Dingcheng.
repairs.after: Daoji led Wang Jing, Shen Linzi and others in a charge against Shao’s army. Shao’s officers and men scattered in alarm and fell back to Dingcheng.

repairs.before: Yao Shao left Yao Luan to choke Tan Daoji's supply line.
repairs.after: Yao Shao left Yao Luan to hold the narrows and cut Tan Daoji’s grain route.

repairs.before: Liu Yu's columns entered from Ziwu and Luogu valleys.
repairs.after: Liu Yu’s detachment commanders Yao Zhen and Dou Ba led separate forces of several thousand men each, Yao Zhen entering by Ziwu and Dou Ba by Luogu.

repairs.before: Yao Hong sent Yao Wan and Yao Qiang to meet them.
repairs.after: Yao Hong sent Yao Wan to oppose Dou Ba and Yao Qiang to oppose Yao Zhen.

repairs.before: Yin Ya was captured by Xu Yan and sent to Liu Yu.
repairs.after: Yao Luan sent his general Yin Ya against Xu Yan, Tan Daoji’s major, south of Tong Pass. Xu Yan captured Yin Ya and sent him to Liu Yu.

repairs.before: Yin Ya said: "You spared me once; now I will not beg like a coward.
repairs.after: Yin Ya said, “Surviving the first time was already more than I had hoped for. How could I be unwilling to die now?

repairs.before: Ya said, "Formerly living was already beyond expectation; now death surely I do not willingly accept.
repairs.after: Yin Ya said, “Surviving the first time was already more than I had hoped for. How could I be unwilling to die now?

repairs.before: You claim to conquer by virtue—do not kill the one Qin man who keeps faith!"
repairs.after: You intend to pacify the realm through great righteousness. How can you deny Qin a minister who keeps faith with his ruler?”

repairs.before: Yao Hong posted Yao Hedou at Yaoliu against Shen Tianzi.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yao Hedu, an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gates, to encamp at Yaoliu as a precaution against Shen Tianzi.

repairs.before: Hong sent attendant gentleman Huangmen Yao Hedou to camp at Yaoliu to prepare for Tianzi.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yao Hedu, an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gates, to encamp at Yaoliu as a precaution against Shen Tianzi.

repairs.before: Yao Shao told his generals: "Jin hugs its walls waiting for reinforcements.
repairs.after: Yao Shao told his generals, “Daoji and the others have come a long way to their deaths. Their forces are small. They cling to their ramparts to defend themselves only because they want to gain time until reinforcements arrive.

repairs.before: Yao Shao said to the generals, "Daoji and others have come from afar to deliver death; their hosts are not many; hugging ramparts and self-fortifying—they only wish to prolong days and months to await follow-up relief.
repairs.after: Yao Shao told his generals, “Daoji and the others have come a long way to their deaths. Their forces are small. They cling to their ramparts to defend themselves only because they want to gain time until reinforcements arrive.

repairs.before: Send a column to Wenxiang to sever their supplies and Tan Daoji's head will be on your pole within a month.
repairs.after: I want to send part of our army back to hold Wenxiang and cut their grain transport. Before a month has passed, Daoji’s head can hang beneath my standard.

repairs.before: Kill Tan Daoji and Liu Yu loses his spear point."
repairs.after: Once Daoji and the others are destroyed, Liu Yu’s plans will come to nothing.”

repairs.before: Yao Shao spread his wings: Hu Yidu on the east plain, Yao Luan on the main road, pressing Jin.
repairs.after: Shao positioned his armies along separate routes so they could support each other. He sent Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to hold the eastern plain and Martial Guard commander Yao Luan to encamp on the main road, in contact with the Jin army.

repairs.before: Shao divided roads and set various armies in horn-and-flank posture, sent General Who Supports the State Hu Yidu to hold the eastern plain, Martial Guard Yao Luan to camp on the great road, connecting with the Jin army.
repairs.after: Shao positioned his armies along separate routes so they could support each other. He sent Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to hold the eastern plain and Martial Guard commander Yao Luan to encamp on the main road, in contact with the Jin army.

repairs.before: Shen Linzi night-attacked; Yao Luan fell with nine thousand men.
repairs.after: Shen Linzi picked elite troops and had them hold gags in their mouths to keep silent during a night attack. Yao Luan’s force broke and he died in battle. More than nine thousand soldiers were killed.

repairs.before: Shen Linzi picked crack troops, held mouthpieces for a night raid; Luan's host broke in battle and died; more than nine thousand soldiers died.
repairs.after: Shen Linzi picked elite troops and had them hold gags in their mouths to keep silent during a night attack. Yao Luan’s force broke and he died in battle. More than nine thousand soldiers were killed.

repairs.before: Yao Zan tried to ship grain from Puban but Jin smashed the train at Xiangcheng.
repairs.after: Yao Zan camped on the Yellow River and sent Yao Nan, General Who Restores Might, to bring grain from Puban to supply his army. When Nan reached Xiangcheng, the Jin army defeated him.

repairs.before: Yao Chen raced to save Yao Nan, missed him, but beat a Jin column in the bend and held Puban.
repairs.after: Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu and Yao Hedu to attack Xue Bo in Hedong. When Hedu heard that the Jin army was intercepting Yao Nan, he hurried by forced marches to help. Nan was defeated before Hedu arrived, but Hedu then defeated a subordinate general of Liu Yu’s at the bend of the Yellow River and camped at Puban.

repairs.before: At the time Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu, Yao Hedou campaigned against Xue Bo in Hedong; hearing the royal army was intercepting Nan, they hurried by combined roads to rescue; before arriving Nan was defeated, yet they broke Liu Yu's lieutenant at the river bend, then camped at Puban.
repairs.after: Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu and Yao Hedu to attack Xue Bo in Hedong. When Hedu heard that the Jin army was intercepting Yao Nan, he hurried by forced marches to help. Nan was defeated before Hedu arrived, but Hedu then defeated a subordinate general of Liu Yu’s at the bend of the Yellow River and camped at Puban.

repairs.after: Yao Shao sent his left chief clerk Yao Qia, Yao Moli and others with three thousand cavalry to camp at Jiuyuan north of the Yellow River. He meant to cut off the tax-grain shipments that the counties were sending Tan Daoji.

repairs.before: Yao Qia refused: "A small force that stands stubborn becomes bait.

repairs.before: Shen Linzi destroyed Yao Qia on the riverbank.

repairs.before: Yao Hong begged Northern Wei for aid against Jin.
repairs.after: As the Jin army pressed closer, Yao Hong sent envoys to Wei to ask for troops.

repairs.after: Wei sent Baba Song, minister of education and Duke of Nanping, and Yizhan Juan, Upright General and Duke of Anping, to advance and occupy Henei. Raiding General Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong to support Hong.

repairs.after: Wei sent Baba Song, minister of education and Duke of Nanping, and Yizhan Juan, Upright General and Duke of Anping, to advance and occupy Henei. Raiding General Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong to support Hong.

repairs.before: Liu Yu halted at Shan city and sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand crack troops over the mountains to join Shen Tianzi and others at Qingni, intending to attack Yaoliu.

repairs.before: Yao Hong marched with Yao Yu to meet them.
repairs.after: Yao Hong sent Yao Yu ahead with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose them. Hong himself led the main army out after him.

repairs.before: Yao Yu lost to Shen Tianzi; Yao Hong fell back to Bashang as towns went over to Jin.
repairs.after: Shen Tianzi defeated Yao Yu. Hong fell back and camped at Bashang, and many commanderies and counties in Guanzhong entered into secret communication with the Jin army.

repairs.after: Shen Tianzi defeated Yao Yu. Hong fell back and camped at Bashang, and many commanderies and counties in Guanzhong entered into secret communication with the Jin army.

repairs.after: Yao Zan opposed Liu Yu west of the pass, and Yao Nan camped at Xiangcheng.

repairs.before: Yu sent Wang Zhen'e and Wang Chong west from Qiushe to cross the Wei, pressing Nan's army.
repairs.after: Liu Yu sent Wang Zhen’e and Wang Jing west from Qiushe to cross the Wei and press Yao Nan’s army.

repairs.before: Yao Pu crushed Jin at Puban; Xu Yi died and Zhu Chaoshi ran.
repairs.after: Yao Pu, General Who Guards the East, and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi and the others at Puban. Xu Yizhi was killed, and Zhu Chaoshi abandoned his men and fled to Tong Pass.

repairs.before: General Who Conquers the East Yao Pu and Yao Hedou defeated Yi and others at Puban; Yi met death; Chaoshi abandoned his host and fled to Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Yao Pu, General Who Guards the East, and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi and the others at Puban. Xu Yizhi was killed, and Zhu Chaoshi abandoned his men and fled to Tong Pass.

repairs.before: Floods blocked Yao Zan from crossing the Wei.
repairs.after: Heavy rains sent the Wei River over its banks, and Yao Zan and the others could not cross to the north.

repairs.before: Wang Zhen'e overtook Yao Nan in the flood season.
repairs.after: Wang Zhen’e advanced by water and by land and overtook Yao Nan.

repairs.before: Yao Hong rushed to Stone Bridge to help.
repairs.after: Hong brought his army back from Bashang and halted at Stone Bridge to support Yao Nan.

repairs.before: Yao Zan fell back to Zheng.
repairs.after: Yao Zan withdrew and encamped at the city of Zheng.

repairs.after: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.

repairs.after: Wang Zhen’e sent Mao Dezu against Yao Qiang. Qiang’s force was routed, and Qiang died in battle. Yao Nan fled back to Chang’an.

repairs.before: Wang Zhen'e shattered Yao Pi at the Wei bridge.
repairs.after: Wang Zhen’e advanced along both banks of the Wei and defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.

repairs.after: Yao Hong came from Xiaoyao Garden to help Yao Pi. The ground was narrow against the river, and when Pi was defeated the men trampled one another as they retreated.

repairs.after: Wang Zhen’e entered through Pingshuo Gate. Yao Hong, Yao Yu and the others fled with several hundred horsemen to Stone Bridge.

repairs.before: Yao Zan's men wept and beat the ground when they heard the news.
repairs.after: When Yao Zan learned of Hong’s defeat, he summoned his officers and men and told them. They all struck the ground with their knives, pushed up their sleeves and wept aloud.

repairs.before: Hu Yidu defected to Liu Yu.
repairs.after: Hu Yidu had already been in secret contact with Liu Yu. That day he abandoned his men and fled to Yu.

repairs.before: Yao Zan could not re-enter the sealed capital.
repairs.after: That night Yao Zan led the armies out to join Hong at Stone Bridge. The Jin army already held all the gates. Zan’s army could not enter, and his men scattered in alarm.

repairs.before: Yao Hong decided to surrender to Liu Yu.
repairs.after: At a loss for any other plan, Yao Hong considered surrendering to Liu Yu.

repairs.after: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The men of Jin will have their way. In the end there will surely be no escape. Death by one’s own hand would be better.”

repairs.before: Yao Fonian leaped from the palace wall.

repairs.after: Hong took his wife and children to the gate of the Jin camp and surrendered.

repairs.after: Yao Zan also surrendered to Liu Yu, leading more than a hundred younger men of the imperial clan. Liu Yu killed them all. The rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangtze.

repairs.before: Yao Hong was executed in the Jiankang market at thirty after two years' reign.
repairs.after: Yao Hong was sent to Jiankang and beheaded in the marketplace. He was thirty years old and had reigned for two years.

repairs.after: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke frankly to its violent ruler Shi Hu and gave loyal counsel at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.

repairs.before: Yizhong crossed from the metal quarter, spoke of returning to the Shi house, raised straight words to a violent lord, spread loyal instruction in a perilous court—his plan for posterity lay in submission; the meaning of his lament is worth praising.
repairs.after: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke frankly to its violent ruler Shi Hu and gave loyal counsel at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.

repairs.before: Yao Xiang matched Sun Ce in dash but marched into tragedy.
repairs.after: Yao Xiang, called Jingguo, showed exceptional courage and talent from his youth and was compared to Sun Ce. A close look at his ability and judgment bears out the comparison. That he went on to take a mistaken path is indeed cause for sorrow.

repairs.before: Yao Chang took up Yao Xiang's legacy, stepped into Fu Jian's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise, and borrowed Murong Chong's edge to settle Hangu and Qin.
repairs.after: Yao Chang, called Jingmao, took up the work left by Yao Yizhong and Yao Xiang. Seizing the occasion of the Fu house’s collapse, he called the regional leaders to his side and extended his dominion. Drawing on the force of Murong Chong’s attack, he secured Hangu and the Qin lands with ease.

repairs.after: Yao Xing, called Zilüe, crushed powerful enemies and carried forward the work his predecessor had begun. With an open mind he sought instruction and made room at his side for worthy men. His affection for his brothers brought harmony to the family, and he governed his subjects by clear rewards and punishments. Men of talent served him with complete devotion, and his fighting men gave their lives for him.

repairs.before: Zilue was able to crush mighty foes, bore the completed prior structure, emptied breast to visit the Way, set aside mat to seek worthies, thickly befriended younger brothers to harmonize kin, clarified rewards and punishments to face those below—heroes exhausted their integrity, claws and fangs gave their lives.

repairs.before: At his height he held the heartland and the west in prosperity few could match.
repairs.after: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo. He won the allegiance of the rival Yan regime and made the regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, the harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those close at hand were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?

repairs.before: He took Fen and Jiang, fell Xu and Luo, treated false Yan as vassal and hedged false Shu, leveled Longyou and quieted Hexi—customs rich, years abundant, far quieted and near gathered—though Chu Zhuang or Qin Mu, how could they surpass!
repairs.after: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo, won the submission of the usurping Yan regime and made the pretended regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those nearby were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?

repairs.before: Then pride undid his caution.
repairs.after: Afterward he gave free rein to his ambitions and boasted of his achievements, taking no thought for future trouble.

repairs.before: He entrusted Liangzhou to Tufa, handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, rejecting remonstrance invited calamity; inner walls rose again and again; war without quiet years, men harbored peril in heart.
repairs.after: He entrusted the capital of Liang to Tufa and granted Shuofang to Helian. His insistence on having his way bred disasters. Frontier cities fell in succession, and his rejection of remonstrance invited calamity. Trouble repeatedly broke out within his own house. There was no year of respite from warfare, and the people felt themselves in danger.

repairs.before: He should have showered his soldiers with thanks—
repairs.after: With such grand designs to pursue, should he not have shown profound favor to his men-at-arms?

repairs.before: How fitting to ride those heroic plans and spread deep favor on armored men—
repairs.after: With such grand designs to pursue, should he not have shown profound favor to his men-at-arms?

repairs.before: —yet he lavished gold on Buddhist monks instead.
repairs.after: Instead he exalted teachings the historian deemed deceptive and paid exceptional honors to Buddhist monks.

repairs.before: He let monasteries swell while taxes bled the hills.
repairs.after: At a time that demanded action he devoted himself to the pursuit of nonaction. Those clad in fine robes and fed on rich food numbered nearly ten thousand. Analyzing the real and discoursing on emptiness became the general fashion.

repairs.before: In a time when action was needed, he practiced non-action's enterprise; gorgeous robes and rich food approached ten thousand; splitting substance they talked emptiness—became custom on the wind.

repairs.after: Reserves were exhausted, and even the hills and forests were taxed. Government fell into neglect and authority was broken. These were the causes. They brought ruin upon themselves; Heaven did not destroy them.

repairs.before: Yao Hong was weak when kin tore the realm apart and Jin struck.
repairs.after: Yao Hong, called Yuanzi, was mediocre and timid. He came to power in the aftermath of upheaval, and as internal troubles intensified, defense against outside enemies ceased.

repairs.before: Jin marched in righteousness and took Chang'an;
repairs.after: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.

repairs.before: The royal army wielded obedience, lowered the pace and descended on Chang'an;
repairs.after: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.

repairs.before: Xiang was truly heroic and resolute; Chang alone was a treacherous champion.
repairs.after: Xiang was indeed heroic and resolute; Chang was an outstanding man of treachery.

repairs.after: Your Highness holds the responsibility of a bulwark of the ruling house. You should consider this deeply.

repairs.after: At the time, Master of Writing Wang Min and Right Assistant Director Guo Bo considered the administration of punishments too lenient and discussed imposing stricter rules. Hong said, “When people are thwarted and humiliated, a fierce spirit rises in them.

provenance.reason: The two offices should be rendered accurately in the parallel literal field; 右丞 specifies the right assistant director.

repairs.before: Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to rescue him; Sheng withdrew.
repairs.after: Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to its relief, and Sheng withdrew.

provenance.reason: The threatened place is Qinzhou, not a named male rescuee. Tongjian 117 also has Qin's rear general come to its aid.

repairs.before: Yao Shao and General Who Captures Barbarians Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia, and others led fifty thousand foot and horse to campaign against Bobo; Yao Hui with ten thousand picked cavalry followed them.
repairs.after: Yao Shao, General Who Campaigns against the Enemy Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia and others led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry against Bobo. Yao Hui followed with ten thousand picked cavalry.

provenance.reason: 征虜 is an expeditionary generalship and does not denote taking captives.

repairs.before: Yao Shao advanced and said, "Your Majesty not forgetting to repay virtue—enfeoffing them is right; the ancients respected the affair and charged them with its beginning—it is possible to wait until next spring, then deliberate."
repairs.after: Yao Shao stepped forward and said, “Your Majesty remembers to repay virtue; enfeoffing them is right. The ancients treated such matters with reverence and made appointments at the beginning of the year. You could wait until next spring and then consider it.”

provenance.reason: The proposed timing in the next clause explains 以始; 'charged them with its beginning' obscures the timing of appointments.

repairs.before: Hong sent Colonel of Agile Cavalry Yan Sheng with three thousand horse to hurry there, Martial Guard Yao Yinan leading ten thousand foot soldiers to assist in guarding Luoyang, and also sent General Who Conquers the East and shepherd of Bingzhou Yao Yi to camp south at Shan ford as sounding support.

provenance.reason: The destination is Jiankang; the marketplace is specifically the site of the beheading.

repairs.before: Before long Jin Grand Commandant Liu Yu commanded the great host to campaign against Hong, halted at Pengcheng, sent General Who Wins the Championship Tan Daoji and General Who Soars like Dragon Wang Zhen'e in from Huai and Fei to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng, General Shen Linzi from Bian into the He to attack Cangyuan.
repairs.after: Before long Liu Yu, grand commandant of Jin, led a great army against Hong and halted at Pengcheng. General Shen Linzi went from the Bian into the Yellow River to attack Cangyuan.

provenance.reason: 冠軍將軍 is the military rank Champion General. Both fields of the only other occurrence of 冠軍 (s0131), and s0080 idiomatic, already use Champion General. The replacement preserves 劉裕’s command, officers and titles, Shen’s separate route and objectives.
